name: Sebastia
description: Sebastia is a hilltop village about 12 kilometres northwest of Nablus in the West Bank, built on the ruins of ancient Samaria, capital of the northern Kingdom of Israel in the 9th century BCE. Herod the Great later rebuilt it as a Roman city and renamed it for Augustus. Today its ruins share the hill with Nabi Yahya Mosque, traditionally held to contain John the Baptist's tomb.
